notes: This audit records related evidence that is not emitted as a detected D06 physical-property observation.
It exists to show that chemistry, thermal inertia and thickness were checked rather than silently ignored.
No value here is used to fill a D06 feature that lacks a registered, measured value.

chemistry_evidence.product: MSL APXS summary and geological context, sols 0-3076

depth_support.notes: Scooped active sand at the surface; APXS samples the upper tens of micrometres.

local_site_coordinates.frame_note: MSL local site coordinates from the PDS CSV. Not a geographic CRS and not WGS84.

chemistry_evidence.notes: Real Mars soil chemistry at an AOI, kept audit-only because D06 has no chemistry feature. Not used to infer any physical property.

thermal_inertia_audit.footprint: Mars; existing D03 Jezero windows are inside the 00N060E tile
thermal_inertia_audit.depth_support: upper few centimetres; no single fixed depth
thermal_inertia_audit.reason_not_used: D06 semantics forbids thermal inertia -> bulk density without a verified physical model and stated conductivity/heat-capacity assumptions. No conversion is applied in this pass.
thermal_inertia_audit.notes: Thermal inertia remains D03 evidence and is not relabeled as D06 density or porosity.

cross_checks.detail: PSR Table 7-IV (density 1.97 g/cm3, porosity 36.5%, friction 49.5 deg, 0-20 cm) matches Gasteiner et al. Dataset_Regolith.csv row 100 (density 1.97, porosity 35-38%, friction 47.5-51.5, depth 0-20 cm).
PSR summary gives ~1 kN/m2; Gasteiner row 101 records 0.94 kPa for the same trench experiment. The record keeps both as a published range.

PSR text notes a direct drill-core density of 1.84 g/cm3 from the same Station 8 area, lower than the SRP-derived 1.97 g/cm3. The SRP estimate depends on Gs=3.1; the discrepancy is preserved as a limitation, not averaged away.
Delage et al. (2024) explicitly state there are no direct density measurements at the InSight site. The 1491 kg/m3 value is model-derived from HP3 thermal conductivity and is flagged as such.
The 30 deg friction angle in Delage et al. (2024) is a fixed model input, not a measured value; friction_angle_deg is therefore no_coverage.
The 5.3 MPa mole penetration resistance is not bearing strength; bearing_strength_kpa is no_coverage and no conversion is applied.

forbidden_derivations_not_performed: DEM roughness or slope -> grain size, cohesion, friction angle or bearing strength
land-cover bare fraction -> regolith thickness or grain size
Earth SoilGrids texture or bulk density -> Moon/Mars properties
thermal inertia -> bulk density without a verified physical model and stated assumptions
1 - bulk_density / 2650 -> porosity without a stated particle density
penetration resistance -> bearing strength without a stated failure criterion and reduction model
literature grain-size scalar -> particle-size distribution without bin fractions, basis and depth
rover wheel slip or trafficability score -> bearing strength
blockers: Moon PSD: no machine-readable bin/fraction table with basis and depth for the Station 8 AOI.
Moon bearing strength: only cone penetration resistance is reported; no bearing-capacity conversion applied.
Mars PSD: no measured site-specific distribution; literature grain-size scalar not converted.
Mars porosity: no direct porosity; no density-to-porosity conversion without particle density and model.
Mars friction angle: only an assumed 30 deg model input, not a measurement.
Mars bearing strength: only mole penetration resistance, not bearing strength.
Regolith thickness: feature not registered in D06 FEATURES_V2; shared change via #141.
Soil chemistry: no D06 chemistry feature; APXS values are audit-only.
